To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cyclopropanation of unsaturated lipids is a simple, rapid and quantitative method for the preparation of derivatives for mass spectral analysis, and that the mass spectral fragmentation patterns are sufficiently distinctive to permit deduction of the original structure of unsaturated fatty acids.
cyclopropanation of unsaturated fatty acid methyl esters can be used to determine the position of the double bonds and to distinguish betweencis and trans double bonds.
the mass spectra of the cyclopropyl esters of monoenes, dienes, and tetraenes are very similar to that of the parent ester, but that those of the dicyclopropane esters are quite different.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a method for the quantitative conversion of unsaturation in lipids to cyclopropane rings, and with the application of mass spectrometry to the identification of the resulting cyclopropane fatty acids.
the synthesis, gas-liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry of cyclopropanated fatty acid methyl esters.
the synthesis, separation and identification of the cyclo-propane derivatives of the fatty acid esters of the common lipids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mass spectral analysis of the cyclopropyl derivatives is a valuable tool for the identification of unsaturated ester mixtures.
the cyclopropanation reaction is a useful technique for the structural determination of unsaturated ester derivatives.
the cyclopropanization reaction is a very useful tool for the structural analysis of unsaturated ester mixtures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mass spectra of the cyclopropyl derivatives are not as informative as might have been hoped, but they are useful for confirming the presence of double bonds and in some cases for determining the number of double bonds present.

cyclopropane esters are very useful for GLC and that mass spectra of these derivatives are very useful for the identification of double bond location in unsaturated esters, but that mass spectra of dicyclo and tricyclopropanates are not useful for this purpose.
mass spectra of the cyclopropyl derivatives are not as useful as GLC retention indices for the determination of the original fatty acid structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of cyclopropanation to convert polyunsaturated esters into cyclopropane esters is a useful tool in lipid analysis.
mass spectrometry of the dicyclopropane derivatives can be used to identify the position of double bonds in esters and the position of the methyl groups of the fatty acid moiety in glycerolipids.
the cyclopropanation method can be used to determine the position of unsaturation in complex lipid mixtures.
